extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials who establish or manage advisory committees; members of the public and counsel seeking to understand FACA requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on establishing, operating, managing, and terminating executive-branch advisory committees consistent with the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) and related GSA/OMB rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of advisory committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any group that the President or agencies establish or use to obtain advice or recommendations and that contains at least one non-federal officer or employee is an 'advisory committee' (FACA §3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory trigger for FACA coverage; the bulletin notes there were 933 active advisory committees in FY 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions to FACA applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA does not apply to certain groups, including groups assembled to provide individual advice or exchange facts or information; groups established by certain agencies and other institutions; and groups that Congress exempts from FACA (FACA §§3, 4; 41 CFR §102-3.40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should check statutory, regulatory, and congressional exemptions when determining whether a group is subject to FACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of FACA
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA is meant to ensure that advisory committees are only formed as necessary; used for proper purposes; and operated in an open, independent, balanced, and cost-effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing guides all establishment, governance, membership, openness, and termination decisions about committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment authority and public-interest finding
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory committee can be established by statute or the President. Agency heads can also establish a committee after finding, in consultation with GSA, that the committee is 'in the public interest in connection with the performance of duties imposed on that agency by law' (FACA §9(a); 41 CFR §102-3.30(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consult with GSA and document the public-interest finding when establishing committees under agency authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory function / limitation on use
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a statute or presidential directive provides otherwise, an advisory committee can only serve an advisory function (FACA §9(b); 41 CFR §102-3.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees should not exercise governmental decisionmaking or operational authority unless a specific statutory or presidential exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance: charter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory committee is governed by a charter that includes, among other things, its mission, duration, and estimated costs and meeting frequency (FACA §9(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charters provide the basic governance framework; agencies commonly add further implementing rules consistent with GSA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership balance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory committee’s membership 'must be fairly balanced' in terms of 'the points of view represented' (41 CFR §102-3.30(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider points of view and functional representation when appointing members; by presidential memorandum, agencies may not appoint lobbyists to serve on advisory committees (75 FR 35955).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management and oversight (OMB and agency-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB sets advisory committee ceilings for agencies and reviews and approves annual agency advisory committee management plans (EO 12838, OMB Circular No. A-135).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency management must track committee counts and submit management plans; GSA provides the regulatory framework (41 CFR Part 102-3) that agencies apply locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness: meeting notice, public access, and records
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory committee ordinarily must publish timely notice of meetings in the Federal Register and open meetings to the public. Interested persons are permitted to appear before and file statements with an advisory committee. Committee records, including reports and meeting minutes, must be made available for public inspection and copying (FACA §10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow Federal Register notice timelines, permit public participation and filings, and ensure recordkeeping and public access to reports and minutes in accordance with FACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and renewal limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory committee terminates no later than two years after its establishment unless the President or a federal officer renews it or Congress provides otherwise (FACA §14; 42 CFR §102-3.30(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must monitor committee life spans and process renewals or terminations consistent with statutory limits and agency/GSA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and conflict-of-interest compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory committee members must comply with applicable ethics and conflict-of-interest laws, including Office of Government Ethics rules (41 CFR §102-3.105(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should apply OGE rules and conflict-of-interest standards to appointments and membership duties; see ACUS recommendations and OGE guidance for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration by the General Services Administration (GSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Services Administration (GSA) has primary responsibility for administering FACA. GSA has published rules, available at 41 CFR Part 102-3, that provide the policy framework that agency heads apply to advisory committees they establish and operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency officials should consult GSA regulations at 41 CFR Part 102-3 for procedural and policy details when implementing FACA requirements.
